topicTitle: 19.1 Electric Potential Energy and Electric Potential
answer: Electric potential energy is the work done by an external agent in bringing a positive test charge q0 from infinity (zero potential energy reference) to a given point in the field, without acceleration: U = $W_{external}$ = -$W_{field}$.

topicTitle: 19.1 Electric Potential Energy and Electric Potential
answer: Electric potential is defined as the electric potential energy per unit charge: $V = \frac{W}{q_0}$ or $V = \frac{U}{q_0}$. Its SI unit is the Volt (V).

topicTitle: 19.1 Electric Potential Energy and Electric Potential
answer: One Volt is the potential difference between two points if one Joule of work is done in moving a positive charge of one Coulomb from one point to the other ($1\text{ V} = 1\text{ J/C}$).

topicTitle: 19.6 Charging and Discharging of a Capacitor
answer: A small RC gives a steep curve, the capacitor charges/discharges rapidly. A large RC gives a flatter, more gradual curve. The time constant tau = RC sets the timescale of the exponential rise or decay visible on the graph.

topicTitle: 19.6 Charging and Discharging of a Capacitor
answer: During charging: Q and V rise exponentially toward their maximum values, while I decays exponentially from I0=V0/R toward zero. During discharging: Q, V, and I all decay exponentially from their initial values toward zero. All curves share the same time constant tau = RC.
